# Additions to Esther Chapter 2 (Addition B) — The LOGOS Bible (Formal Equivalent)
**Translator:** LOGOS | **Source:** Codex Vaticanus, Additions to Esther B | **Source Image:** source-texts/greek-DC/ADE_002_page_001.jpg

---

*[Addition B: The full text of King Artaxerxes's genocidal edict. Inserted after Hebrew Esther 3:13. The Greek adds this document to explain what the Hebrew merely summarizes.]*

**1** The following is a copy of the letter: "The Great King Artaxerxes writes to the governors of the one hundred and twenty-seven provinces, from India to Ethiopia, and to their subordinate officials as follows:

**2** Having become master of many nations and obtained dominion over the whole world, I resolved — not puffed up by the arrogance of power, but consistently governing with fairness and gentleness —

**3** to establish for my subjects a life of unbroken tranquility, and to make my kingdom peaceful, civilized, and accessible to all, thereby renewing the peace that all people desire.

**4** When I inquired of my advisors how this goal could be achieved, Haman — who stands foremost among us in sound judgment, has shown himself proven in steadfast goodwill and unwavering loyalty, and holds the second rank in the kingdom —

**5** pointed out to us that there is scattered among all the nations a certain hostile people, whose laws are contrary to those of every other nation, and who consistently disregard royal commands, so that the blameless administration of our kingdom, which we conduct with such distinction, cannot be brought to completion.

**6** Understanding, therefore, that this nation alone is perpetually in opposition to all humanity, conducting itself according to alien laws, and hostile to our governance, working whatever evil it can, and not practicing the virtues of the state,

**7** we command that all those indicated to you in the letters of Haman, who is placed in charge of our affairs and is as a second father to us — all of them together with their wives and children — be utterly destroyed by the swords of their enemies, without pity or mercy, on the fourteenth day of the twelfth month, that is Adar, of the current year,

**8** so that those who have long been hostile and remain so today may in a single day descend by violence to Hades, leaving our affairs stable and undisturbed from that point forward."
